#_aboutJumboText: OCADVersioner helps you create and compare versions of your OCAD map in a simple and clear way.
#_aboutLocalText: OCADVersioner is a program that runs in the browser and does not need to be installed. Everything happens locally on your device, and no map files are uploaded to a server.
#_aboutDiffTitle: See what has changed in your map
#_aboutDiffText: The split view of the map lets you easily see which symbols have been added between versions
#_aboutHowItWorks1: OCADVersioner assumes that the OCAD file you want to version is saved in its own folder for the map project. You choose this folder at startup. By doing so, you give the browser read and write access to the files in the folder.
#_aboutHowItWorks2: After you choose the project folder where the map file is saved, the map is loaded. OCADVersioner has now created an empty folder called "Releases" in the project folder. This is the only folder OCADVersioner will read from and write to, so you can safely keep other files in the project folder or create folders with other names.
#_aboutHowItWorks3: Once the map is loaded, you are ready to create the first version of the map. Since there are no other versions of the map, the map is compared with an empty map file.
#_aboutHowItWorks4: When you create a new version of the map, OCADVersioner copies the map file into a folder under Releases called V1. V1.ocd is the OCAD file as it looked when the version was made. V1.json is an index file used internally by OCADVersioner.
#_aboutHowItWorks5: When you now save changes in OCAD, OCADVersioner detects them and compares the symbols in the selected map file with the latest version you created.
#_aboutHowItWorks6: This table shows which symbols have changed between the versions. This gives you an easy overview of what has been done since last time, and lets you check that what has been added, deleted and edited matches what was done since the previous version.
#_aboutSupportedBrowsersText: OCADVersioner uses the File System API to read and write files locally on your device. This is supported by the most popular browsers. Here is an overview of which browsers support this API, and can therefore use OCADVersioner.
#_aboutCreditsText: Maps are parsed and rendered by Purple Pen's map engine, compiled to WebAssembly and running entirely in your browser. The OCAD parser and renderer come from Purple Pen by Peter Golde, used under the BSD 3-Clause licence. The map viewport is Leaflet. Full notices for every third-party component are in third-party notices. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Purple Pen or Peter Golde.
#_aboutTelemetryText: When this app is deployed with monitoring configured, anonymous usage and error reports are sent to the maintainers so faults can be found and fixed. That covers which pages were opened and what went wrong — never the contents of your maps. Running it locally sends nothing at all.
